text.p: Italian tire and cable company Pirelli announced a near-doubling of first half profits on Thursday as its tire business rebounded and its cables operations continued to thrive and grow.
The Milan-based company said first-half 1996 consolidated net profits rose to 206 billion lire ($136 million) from 115 billion ($75 million) despite a half-year overall sales drop of 3.5 percent.

Pirelli said it now expects better results for 1996 compared to 1995. "We have all the means to be able to continue the course that is starting to give positive results," said group managing director Marco Trochetti Provera at a news conference.
Analysts said the results were led by the rapid recovery of the tire business, and showed solid underlying progress in Pirelli's specialist cables business around the world.
The group's automotive tire interests, grouped under Amsterdam-listed Pirelli-Tire and 81 percent owned by Pirelli SpA, showed profits have soared.
Tire first half net profits rose to 55.4 million guilders ($32.43 million) from 10.7 million guilders ($6.26 million).
"The expectation is that the positive trend in results will continue in the second half, to the same degree as the market," Pirelli-Tyre said in a statement.

Pirelli cable's future prospects were highlighted by the announcement of a long-awaited Chinese joint venture last month which will tap the growth in the rapidily-expanding Chinese telecommunications market.
